references.text: The righteous is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season - 'whatever he does prospers'. This parallels how the Lord was with Joseph and made everything he did succeed.
God reveals himself to Isaac and says 'I am with you and will bless you' - the same pattern of God's presence and blessing we see in Joseph's life.
God's promise to Jacob to be with him wherever he goes reflects the same divine presence that followed Joseph in Egypt.
Even in prison, the Lord was with Joseph and showed him faithful love, demonstrating that God's presence continued regardless of Joseph's external circumstances.
Stephen testifies that God was with Joseph and rescued him from all his troubles, a direct confirmation of what is described in Gen 39:2.
The Lord promises Joshua: 'Be strong and courageous, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.' This mirrors the same promise of God's presence that Joseph experienced.
New Testament confirmation that God's presence was the decisive factor throughout Joseph's story of suffering.
A theological parallel showing God's pattern of granting favor to his chosen one among the Egyptians to accomplish a work of salvation.
A clear theological parallel establishing 'the Lord was with' as the universal source of success for God's chosen ones.
